current.text: Verify that, if the application relies on the CORS preflight mechanism to prevent disallowed cross-origin use of sensitive functionality, it is not possible to call the functionality with a request which does not trigger a CORS-preflight request. This may require checking the values of the 'Origin' and 'Content-Type' request header fields or using an extra header field that is not a CORS-safelisted header-field.

master.text: Verify that, if the application relies on the CORS preflight mechanism to prevent disallowed cross-origin use of sensitive functionality, it is not possible to call the functionality with a request which does not trigger a CORS-preflight request. This may require checking the values of the 'Origin' and 'Content-Type' request header fields or using an extra header field that is not a CORS-safelisted header-field.

predecessors.text: Verify that REST services explicitly check the incoming Content-Type to be the expected one, such as application/xml or application/json.

Verify that the Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) Access-Control-Allow-Origin header uses a strict allow list of trusted domains and subdomains to match against and does not support the "null" origin.

Verify that RESTful web services that utilize cookies are protected from Cross-Site Request Forgery via the use of at least one or more of the following: double submit cookie pattern, CSRF nonces, or Origin request header checks.

summaries.body:
The 5.0.0 mapping records V3.5.2 as MODIFIED, moved from 4.0.3 V13.2.5, split from V14.5.3, and covering V13.2.3. Those predecessors required REST services to check incoming Content-Type, CORS ACAO against a strict allow list (no "null" origin), and cookie-using REST CSRF protections (double-submit, nonces, or Origin). The current clause is the complementary CORS-preflight branch: if the application relies on preflight to block disallowed cross-origin use of sensitive functionality, that functionality must not be callable with a request that skips preflight (Origin/Content-Type checks or an extra non-safelisted header).

The mapping notes that predecessor text is dissimilar and that git/content lineage diverges from the ID slot. Git on V13.2.5/V13.2.3 is 4.0 API-chapter work; stamps on V3.5.2 are old session-management occupancy. Mapping and the three predecessor texts are the reliable origin.

The attested 5.0 change folds Content-Type checking, CORS allowlisting, and REST CSRF into a single preflight-integrity rule. Named 4.0 mechanisms (double-submit, "null" origin, xml/json Content-Type examples) are not restated. #475/#566 and ronperris's #357 typo fix are 4.0 events on the REST predecessors.

Grammarly, number-formatting of V13, and session-management CWEs on the V3.5.2 number did not rewrite this preflight clause.
